newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen earnings seen under pressure in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Loewen earnings seen under pressure in Q2.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc may be hard pressed to meet consensus second-quarter earnings forecasts from its normal operations when the funeral home chain releases results Monday because of industry-wide weakness, analysts said.
According to a survey of estimates by First Call, Loewen is expected to announce second quarter earnings of US$0.37 a share, up from US$0.30 a share a year ago.
But analysts said an unexpected drop in the death rate created tough conditions in the second quarter for Loewen, North America's second-biggest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries.

"I have an estimate of 37 cents but I'm a little skeptical about their ability to earn that level from normal operations. A more realistic level (of operating earnings) looks to me like 33 cents," said one analyst who declined to be identified.
"It was a tough quarter. Mortality was low and the number of deaths was down about three percent," the analyst said.

Texas-based Service Corp International -- Loewen's chief rival and the industry's biggest operator -- also cited industry softness when it announced second-quarter results last month. But it managed to boost its earnings to US$0.32 a share from US$0.26 a share by controlling costs.
Loewen officials were not available for comment but analysts said the company has told them the consensus estimates were reasonable.
As a result, some analysts will look for unusual items or a reliance on so-called pre-need sales from Loewen's cemetery business that help the company meet the US$0.37 consensus.
"To get to 37 cents, they may need to do something creative," said another analyst who also declined to be identified.

Analysts said Loewen has been aggressively trying to boost sales of plots, monuments and other items to individuals making advance arrangements for their own deaths -- so-called "pre-need" sales. Those revenues can be booked immediately in its cemetery business.

In addition Loewen has reportedly sold 18 funeral homes in Wisconsin to a group of investors, expecting the state will force the divestiture because of a rule that bars companies from owning both funeral homes and cemeteries.
For Loewen, the Wisconsin deal could well result in a special gain in the second quarter, analysts said. The rule is being challenged in court, they said.

In addition, Loewen is rumored to be closing its office in Cincinnati as a long-term cost-saving measure and this could result in a charge for the quarter, analysts said. Loewen also continues to be burdened by high legal expenses.

Given its earnings challenges, Loewen may have trouble meeting analysts' estimates for the year of US$1.55 to US$1.60 a share, even though it has said those are reasonable, analysts said. Skepticism among investors about earnings growth has weighed on its stock price, they said.
